label: Fourteen finite tests of rivals of the stage-two attribute premises
paraphrase: Closed mathematical controls: fourteen finite interpretations on one- or two-element carriers, one per stage-two attribute premise. In each, the recorded rival of the premise holds, every other premise of the named consuming theorem holds, and that theorem's conclusion fails. (1) Actuality without being: the one existent is in act in a non-esse respect only; every existent is in act in some respect; not every existent is in act in esse. (2) Emergent perfection: one being causes another to be and to have a second perfection which the cause lacks; every caused perfection is had by the effect; the cause of being does not have what it gives. (3) Actuality without goodness: the one being is God, maximal in being, in act and good in nothing; God is not supremely good. (4) Uncaused composite: the one being is God, maximal, composite and caused by nothing; God is not simple. (5) Esse-essence difference without composition: an unmoved mover whose act of being differs from its essence, with nothing composite; the first mover is not simple in the encoded sense. (6) A first being that is a component: at one world a necessary actual root is first and potency-free and is a component of a distinct composite whole; no actual root is first and a component of nothing. (7) Material intellect: God is immaterial, maximal and first and lacks intellect, while a matter-form composite has intellect; God does not have intellect. (8) Intellect without will: the one being is God with intellect and no will. (9) Potency prior to act: the one being is in potency, nothing is in act or prior; a first being is in potency. (10) Act and potency in one respect: the one being is in act and in potency in the one respect and simply prior to itself; a first being is in potency. (11) Finite subsistent being: a simple unmoved mover whose act of being is its essence, not infinite, lacking a pure perfection. (12) Immutable without eternity: the one being is God, maximal, first, in potency in no respect and not eternal. (13) Naming: the one being meets the full nominal description, the practice's name refers to no being, proper application is preserved by reference vacuously, and the naming leaf fails; the full description is not excluded. (14) The nine attributes falling short: the one being is God with all nine predicates and the other thirteen non-logical premises hold, while the primitive classical-attributes field is false of it. The general logical premise excluded middle of two consuming theorems is not part of any interpretation and is not checked. These are statements about fourteen finite interpretations only; none shows a rival true or a premise false.
